chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Writing songs with Johnny
summary: The brothers collaborated, with Reb suggesting melodies and Johnny writing them down; since Johnny's death Reb writes his own.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: We ought to get more...we don't have really a mention of more of your songs. Uh, in most cases...
Oh, I...we got a hundred of them over there.
In most cases, were you the lyric writer, or did you and your brother collaborate on both the words and the music?

Well, he was mostly...since he died, I been writing my own music, but when they...when he was living, he done most of the...you know, he was a good piano player. We collaborate on the songs, and I'd say, "Well, I don't like that," I'd sing over it: "Dee-dit-dit-dood-dood-do-dat-do-do" [singing illustration]"Now, you write it
like that," and he...then he'd write it, and I'd give him the melody that I liked, but since he's passed, I sit down on the piano and jab 'em out myself.
But in the...when you were collaborating, you collaborated on both parts--both the words and the...
You both worked on both parts?

Yeah. If I didn't like the kind of melody he had, why I would suggest him something else, you know. See, here's where I had my own mortgage company. That was when...[crashing sound of Spikes microphone falling].
